messages.author: 223beb57ce203bde
messages.subject: hexbin and facets
parts:
Dear All,

How can I get the same sizes of hexagons across facets? For example:

library(ggplot2)
set.seed(10)
df <- data.frame(
x = rnorm(1000), y = rnorm(1000),
z = rep(1:2, times = c(980, 20)))
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + geom_hex(bins = 20) + facet_grid(z~.)

It seems the actual data range in each panel is used to calculate the
binwidth? How can I force hexbin to calculate binwidth using the
displayed xlim and ylim?

Thanks a lot for any help.

Regards,
Xie Chao

messages.author: 223beb57ce203bde
messages.subject: Re: hexbin and facets
parts:
I found one workaround:
1) expand the data frame, so that all facets have the same xy data limits
2) set x and y limit using the coord_cartesian, so that the expanded
data are ignored and the original data are included

xie chao

Hi Hadley,

Thank you for the reply. However, it seems that there is no binwidth
parameter in geom_hex?

> ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + geom_hex(binwidth = 0.6) + facet_grid(z~.)
Error in if (diff(ybnds) <= 0) stop("ybnds[1] < ybnds[2] is not fulfilled") :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Even if binwidth works in geom_hex, how can I handle different scales
in X and Y (say X ranges from 1 to 1000 while Y ranges from 0 to 0.1)?

Xie Chao
